message.content: Lion and zebra are both placental mammals, so their most recent common ancestor is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria). This ancestor lived roughly 55–60 million years ago, before the lineages that would become the order **Carnivora** (lion) and the order **Perissodactyla** (zebra) split apart.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want the common ancestor. We need to answer. There's no tool needed. Just provide answer. Probably mention that both belong to order Carnivora (lion) and order Perissodactyla (zebra). But they share a common ancestor at the level of mammals. The common ancestor would be a mammal from the Eutheria clade. The last common ancestor of all placental mammals. So answer: the last common ancestor of all placental mammals. Or maybe more specific: the last common ancestor of the two species is the ancestor of the family Felidae and Equidae, which diverged from the common ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That ancestor lived about 55 million years ago. So answer accordingly.
